title: Recurrence Set Evaluation Order ((RRULE union RDATE) minus EXDATE) and Deduplication

citations.verbatim_quote: The final recurrence set is generated by gathering all of the start DATE-TIME values generated by any of the specified "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, and then excluding any start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties. This implies that start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties take precedence over those specified by inclusion properties (i.e., "RDATE" and "RRULE"). When duplicate instances are generated by the "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, only one recurrence is considered. Duplicate instances are ignored.

The "EXDATE" property can be used to exclude the value specified in "DTSTART". However, in such cases, the original "DTSTART" date MUST still be maintained by the calendaring and scheduling system because the original "DTSTART" value has inherent usage dependencies by other properties such as the "RECURRENCE-ID".

The recurrence set is the complete set of instances for an object. It is generated by considering the following properties in order, all of which are optional: 1. The "recurrenceRules" property (Section 4.3.3) generates a set of extra date-times on which the object occurs. 2. The "excludedRecurrenceRules" property (Section 4.3.4) generates a set of date-times that are to be removed from the previously generated set of date-times on which the object occurs. 3. The "recurrenceOverrides" property (Section 4.3.5) defines date- times that are added or excluded to form the final set.

rationale: RFC 5545 Sections 3.8.5.1, 3.8.5.2, and 3.8.5.3 (and RFC 8984 Section 4.3) define the recurrence set of a recurring component as the union of candidate occurrences generated from DTSTART + RRULE and RDATE (deduplicating any identical start values across RRULE and RDATE), followed by set subtraction of any occurrences matching EXDATE. Consequently, EXDATE takes strict precedence over both RRULE and RDATE, a component with RDATE (even without RRULE) is a recurring component, and excluding the initial DTSTART instance via EXDATE removes only that instance from expansion while preserving the original DTSTART property on the master component.
store_implication: On calendar component state and timeline expansion: (1) Recurrence expansion MUST union RRULE and RDATE occurrences, deduplicate identical occurrence start times, and remove any occurrence present in EXDATE. (2) Single-instance operations (deletion or modification of an individual occurrence) MUST work uniformly whether the targeted occurrence originates from RRULE, RDATE, or both, including on RDATE-only recurring components (where RRULE is absent and RDATE is non-empty). (3) Deleting the first occurrence (where RECURRENCE-ID equals DTSTART) as a single instance MUST append DTSTART to the master component's EXDATE set while keeping the master component's DTSTART property unchanged.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: An RDATE matches an occurrence already generated by RRULE: only one instance is emitted on the expanded timeline, and a single EXDATE for that start time removes the occurrence completely.

Excluding the initial DTSTART occurrence via a single-instance deletion: the master component's DTSTART property MUST remain intact so future RRULE evaluation and RECURRENCE-ID references remain anchored to the original DTSTART.

A component recurring solely via RDATE (no RRULE): deleting or editing a single occurrence MUST add an EXDATE (or create a RECURRENCE-ID override on edit) rather than deleting or overwriting the entire component.
Excluding every candidate occurrence generated by RRULE and RDATE via EXDATE results in an empty timeline expansion while keeping the master component stored with its original DTSTART.

scenarios.name: delete_rdate_and_first_instance_on_rrule_series
scenarios.description: Deleting the initial DTSTART occurrence of a series with both RRULE and RDATE preserves the master DTSTART and suppresses that occurrence from the timeline via EXDATE while deduplicating overlapping RRULE and RDATE occurrences.

scenarios.name: delete_single_instance_on_rdate_only_component
scenarios.description: Deleting a single occurrence of a component that recurs via RDATE without RRULE adds an EXDATE instead of deleting the entire component.
